title: Storage backends
description: Choose local disk or an S3 bucket while keeping the same client-facing API.

sections.title: Local disk
paragraphs: Without LOFT_BUCKET, the API uses the disk backend. LOFT_DATA selects the root directory and defaults to .loft-data. Persist and back up the whole directory, including metadata and links.

sections.title: S3 storage
paragraphs: Set LOFT_BUCKET to enable the S3 backend. AWS_REGION defaults to us-east-1. Credentials come from AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY as configured for Bun’s S3 client. AWS_ENDPOINT can select an S3-compatible endpoint.
sections.code:
export LOFT_BUCKET="your-loft-bucket"
export AWS_REGION="us-east-1"
# Supply AWS credentials through your deployment environment.
bun --filter @loft/api dev

sections.title: Preserve metadata and links
paragraphs: A file’s bytes, metadata, and issued-link records form the store. Copying object bytes alone is not a complete backup. There is no automatic migration when you change backends.
Run one writer per store, and verify restore procedures before relying on the installation for your only copy of important files.

sections.title: AWS infrastructure
paragraphs: The repository includes Terraform in infra/aws for a private bucket, CloudFront, ECR, and an optional ECS Fargate service behind an ALB. The service starts with desired count zero until an image is published.
Review the infrastructure and its costs before applying it. Set loft_token explicitly, publish the API image to the created ECR repository, and use your own HTTPS origin for clients.
